content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods (e.g., 2024-04-04, 2024-04-05) and overestimates in later periods (e.g., 2024-04-17, 2024-05-20).
- Forecasts show strong upward bias after spikes in history (e.g., 38.18 → 38.48, 38.56 → 41.53), suggesting model fails to cap or reset after sharp rises.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts often overshoot recent highs and then correct downward, but true outcomes show stronger persistence or delayed correction.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days in early periods, especially when prices are volatile or trending upward.
- Model overreacts to recent high values (e.g., 38.56 → 42.10, 42.11 → 43.18), suggesting failure to account for structural or seasonal factors.
- In periods of sustained upward trend (e.g., 2024-05-20), model fails to capture the full magnitude of the breakout, underestimating peak values.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp drops or sudden spikes in true outcomes.
- Forecasts often underestimate the true mean of the 30-day window, especially when true values are higher than historical average.
